Hassanzadeh2026_10-47176-pd-2026-1561.reason: The cover is a chemical monolayer: a hexadecanol anti-evaporation film. It is not a floating or suspended cover made of discrete elements. Protocol section 3 lists chemical monolayers and continuous covers as context or comparison only, so they are not part of the S/phi dataset. The screening decision ('include', phi 1) is overridden for that reason. The paper also gives no partial-coverage fraction, and the film is assumed to cover the whole surface.
Hassanzadeh2026_10-47176-pd-2026-1561.notes: Contextual values from the full text (no rows extracted, because this is a monolayer). The Persian numbers were checked on rendered PDF pages 5, 7, 8 and 10, because the .txt reverses Persian decimals. Experiment: a Class A pan treated with hexadecanol was compared with an untreated control pan over 16 days. Air speed, temperature and RH were logged three times a day (abstract; section 3, p. 9). The hexadecanol dose and the site are not reported. The authors are based in Tehran (BSk) and Dezful, but the experiment location is not stated, so climate is left blank. CFD model: VOF in ANSYS Fluent with 4 phases (water, air, vapour, hexadecanol), 10:1 scaled geometry and 24 simulated minutes. The model was run at 35-40 degC, RH 15-20% and 'usual' wind speed (p. 10). In the mesh study (Table 1, p. 9), Case 4 has 1 mm cells, 299,025 nodes and 0.02599 kg. The English summary wrongly gives 0.5 mm, which is Case 5. The reported comparison is in Figs 10-11 (p. 10). Without coating: numerical 0.10829 kg vs experimental 0.09415 kg, a 12% difference. With hexadecanol: numerical 0.02599 kg vs experimental 0.02261 kg, a 13% difference. The hexadecanol experimental value comes from a 0.23 mm level drop in the real treated pan over 24 min, converted to 0.2261 kg and divided by 10 for the 10:1 scale. The authors state that the laboratory evaporation rate is a daily average (p. 10), so the 24-min 'experimental' curves are derived from daily means, not measured over 24 min. Taken at face value, the treated pan would lose about 13.8 mm d-1 and the untreated one about 50 mm d-1, which is implausible for a Class A pan. Implied S = 1 - 0.02261/0.09415 = 0.76 (experiment) and 1 - 0.02599/0.10829 = 0.76 (model), which matches the reported ~76%. The text says the model reduction is below 20% in the first 10 min and extrapolates it to 85% after 4 h (p. 11). However, Fig. 12 suggests about 50% at 10 min. The paper is internally inconsistent about the geometry. The initial water depth is 2.4 cm in the English abstract but 4.2 cm in the Persian abstract (p. 5). The English extended summary (p. 2) gives a 4.2 cm diameter and height with a 4.2 cm water depth. The Persian method (section 2-4, pp. 7-8) gives a model vessel 10 cm in diameter and 2.4 cm high. The DOI on the Persian page (10.47176/pd.2026.1558) also differs from the English page (10.47176/pd.2026.1561). The 16-day experiment is reported only as a 24-minute equivalent, so the period and measurement appraisals are high risk.

Table 2 gives percentages 'relative to ideal'. Back-calculating (reduction / percentage) gives a constant reference of about 4228 mm/yr (about 11.58 mm/d, roughly the regression E at W = 19 m/s), so the percentage is read as S = dE/E_o for the lee surface. E_o and E_c are left null because only the reduction is reported. Wind speed recovers fully about 9H (22.5 m) behind the panel; the authors say another panel row is needed within 9H, but no array or phi is specified. Table 3 gives energy yield (taken from ref. 11, Mondol et al. 2007) and Table 4 a combined objective. The optimum is azimuth 30 deg (NW, facing wind) with tilt 30 deg: S 71.36% and energy efficiency 99.45%. The best evaporation scenario is azimuth 0 / tilt 60 (90.25%). Related earlier paper by the same group on windbreaks at the same site: Hashemi Monfared, Rezapour & Zhian 2018, Iranian J. Ecohydrology, p. 265. It uses a different windbreak and is not the same data. The three Chah Nimeh reservoirs together cover 47 km2; the area of Chah Nimeh 4 alone is not given.

S2019_10-24200-j30-2017-4935-2183.notes: Persian paper. The extracted text is garbled, so it was read from rendered PDF page images. Model-only study of daily evaporation from the Ostad Esteghlal Minab dam reservoir (Hormozgan, Iran). The lake area is about 20 km2 at normal level (stated p. 30) and total volume 350 MCM. The period is SH 1390-1394 (about March 2011 to March 2016, 1826 days), with Bandar Abbas/Jask station data. Evaporation uses Penman-Monteith with heat storage and de Bruin (1982) water temperature. Aerodynamic resistance r_a uses the Calder & Neal wind function with U10 and lake area. The cetyl alcohol monolayer is an added resistance, r_m = 300 - 44.74U (s m-1) for U < 6.71 m s-1 and 0 above. The monolayer is assumed continuously present on the whole surface (re-applied every 1-3 days), so phi = 1 is an assumption, not a measurement. Wind-driven film loss is represented only through the r_m(U) decline. Annual S, State 1 (year-round): 1390 7.8%, 1391 8.3%, 1392 7.9%, 1393 8.2%, 1394 6.8%. State 2 (summer only): 2.46%, 3.1%, 2.41%, 2.38%, 1.26%. Annual base / State 1 / State 2 evaporation (mm): 1390 2029/1872/1979; 1391 2226/2042/2157; 1392 2124/1957/2073; 1393 2271/2086/2217; 1394 2226/2057/2198 (Table 4, re-decoded by second reviewer). Mean annual saving is 177 mm (3.54 MCM) in State 1 and 58 mm (1.16 MCM) in State 2 (Table 5). The tables are internally inconsistent. The base-case column sums to 10876, not the reported 10916, so the reported mean of 2183 is slightly high. The 1394 State-1 value of 2057 does not fit its 6.8%; 2075 would match both the 6.8% and the column sum of 10032. The paper's means (8.1%, 2.7%) are kept. Corrected means would be about 7.8% and 2.3%. Table 2 lists literature monolayer reductions (other studies, not rows). Table 6 is a WaterSavr cost analysis. This is a chemical monolayer, not a partial physical cover: decision context_only per protocol.

Rodrigues2023_10-21203-rs-3-rs-2521923-v.reason: Remote-sensing study (calibrated Stephens-Stewart equation on Landsat scenes) of Santo Anastacio reservoir: reports the percent reduction of modelled evaporation rate on 5 dates with floating macrophyte cover (phi 0.30-0.70 from k-means classification) relative to the mean of 5 macrophyte-free dates. Model-based estimate with a non-concurrent reference; S refers to the rate per unit open-water area.
Rodrigues2023_10-21203-rs-3-rs-2521923-v.notes: Research Square preprint (v1, Feb 2023); I did not check whether a peer-reviewed version exists. The second reservoir, Pacoti, had no macrophytes and serves only for model validation, so it gives no rows. Evaporation is the mean of open-water pixels: Fig. 4 is titled 'evaporation from free water surface', and in Table 3 the evaporated volume equals the rate times the open-water area (e.g. 1995: 285 m3/d = 5.7 mm/d x 0.05 km2). The macrophyte pixels are therefore excluded and macrophyte evapotranspiration is not counted. The reported reductions compare the per-open-area rate on macrophyte dates (1995-2015) with the 2008 macrophyte-free dates, so they mix date/season effects with the cover effect. The Stephens-Stewart equation has no macrophyte physics and is driven only by LST-derived air temperature and shortwave radiation. Pooled result: evaporation is 10.7% lower on macrophyte days (about 11% in the abstract). This pooled value is not entered as a separate row to avoid double counting. The preprint is internally inconsistent: (1) the per-date rates in Table 3 (1995 5.7, 2005 6.3, Feb-2008 5.8, May-2008 6.1, 2015 6.2 mm/d; macrophyte-free mean 6.5) do not reproduce the reported reductions, whereas the Fig. 8a points do (Fig. 8a regression intercept 6.67 mm/d); (2) the MC values in Fig. 8 (about 24, 24, 31, 43, 68%) differ slightly from the Fig. 5 labels (30, 30, 45, 70%); (3) the text says the small area on Feb 10, 2008 was a sensor failure, yet counts that date as a macrophyte date. Reference: CAPW Class A pan in a floating tank, Kp 0.95. Validation RMSE 0.8 mm/d, which is similar in size to the 0.4-1.1 mm/d differences attributed to macrophytes.

Daud2023_10-1088-1755-1315-1205-1-012017.reason: Field experiment with three identical aluminium pans side by side (uncovered, and 46.08% and 92.16% ping-pong-ball cover) at UiTM Shah Alam over 28 daytime observation periods; the paper reports the reduction of total evaporation (52.05% and 77.63%).
Daud2023_10-1088-1755-1315-1205-1-012017.notes: Pan geometry is inconsistent: the abstract says 225 mm diameter and 80 mm 'width', but Fig. 2 shows a 250 mm diameter pan, 80 mm high, with 30 mm water depth. The reported phi equals N x (40/250)^2: 36 balls give 0.9216 and 18 give 0.4608. So phi is the projected area of standard 40 mm balls over a 250 mm pan, and 250 mm was used. The text swaps the ball counts ('36 and 18 respectively'); the arithmetic shows 18 balls for 46.08% and 36 for 92.16%. Thirty-six 40 mm circles cannot form a monolayer in a 250 mm circle (the densest known packing needs R/r of about 6.76, against 6.25 here; at most about 30 fit), so the real projected cover of the 92.16% pan was probably at most about 0.77, with balls riding up. The abstract values (6, 3 and 2 mm) are maximum 12-h totals and give S of about 0.50 and 0.67; these are not used. The reported S (52.05% and 77.63%) is reproduced exactly by the 28-day sums of the daily rates in Fig. 4: U 9.121, C46 4.374, C92 2.035 mm/h-days, giving S 0.5205 and 0.7769. Readings were taken with a ruler at 4-h intervals from 08:00 to 20:00 only; the values come in steps of 0.5 mm per 12 h, and rain was handled from the level changes. There was one pan per condition, inside wire-mesh cages on a wooden platform on the ground. Table 1 values come from other studies and were not extracted.

The authors state that the forcing reduction produced by a given FPV coverage is unknown and design-dependent, so phi is undefined; the only proxy is the forcing-reduction fraction on the 1:1 line, which is said to approximate floating solar coverage. It uses 2009 meteorology only, with wind at 10 m and T/RH at 2 m. Numerical results (Table S2) are in the supplementary material, which is not available. Values were digitised by colour-matching heatmap pixels just above and below the solid 1:1 line in Fig. 2a (annual evaporation, colourbar +75 to -375 mm/yr) and Fig. 2b (% change, colourbar 0 to about -120%), using the embedded figure image and the colourbar tick labels; second reviewer's re-digitisation gives panel agreement within about 1.5 percentage points at all extracted levels (10%: 0.176/0.179; 25%: 0.44/0.43; 50%: 0.80/0.79; 90%: 1.07/1.075). The text reports that at a 74% 1:1 reduction annual net evaporation crosses zero (dew deposition gives a net water gain), so S >= 1 beyond that point; the Discussion (p. 16, manuscript lines 425-426) words this as 'coverages greater than 74 % (1:1 forcing variable reduction)', i.e. the authors loosely equate the 1:1 reduction with coverage, but elsewhere (Methods, lines 164-165) they state that the forcing change for a given coverage is unknown. Wind-dominant and solar-dominant scenario lines were not extracted; the text says scenarios where solar is reduced more than wind give larger evaporation reductions. If the review accepts the forcing-reduction fraction as a phi proxy, use the condition value. S > 1 reflects the model's net condensation.

de2023_t-cnicas-de-redu-o-da-evapora-o-e.notes: MSc thesis, Melo 2023 (UFPE). Phase 1 continues the Nascimento 2021 installation at UFPE/CAA Caruaru with new data: 22 Jan 2021 to 30 Dec 2022, 61 weekly readings. It is the same installation, so same_study_as is filled, but it is not a duplicate. Phase 1 boxes measure 0.37 x 0.56 x 0.13 m (p.51). Phase 2 (IPA Caruaru, 17 Mar to 22 Jun 2023, rainy season, 8 fortnightly readings) used buried 500 L polyethylene tanks: rim diameter 1.22 m, base 0.95 m, depth 0.58 m. Phase 2 covers were TPG, clear PET with 125 mL water, and tetrapak. EVAPORATION METHOD (pp.58-59): Eq. 25 subtracts P, but the author states that precipitation was NOT taken into account, and negative net values (rain gains) were set to zero. Screens partly intercept rain and the tetrapak-covered tank receives none, which biases comparisons in rainy periods. PET phi is not restated here; the values come from Nascimento 2021 (green 0.728, clear 0.744). Melo swaps the bottle volumes (green 250 mL, clear 200 mL; 95 and 145 mL of water). Screens: TPP = small aperture (80% shading), TPG = large aperture (50%), TV/TB = mosquito mesh (14%); phi = nominal shade fraction. Tetrapak covers were frequently replaced, while the PET bottles aged (became opaque and deformed). Seasonal rows (Tables 9-12, 53, 64, 75) are given for the PET bottles only, to stay within the row limit. Tetrapak was the best cover in every season (29-66%). Monthly values for all covers are in Table 8.
